# Issue review

## Scope

All 124 issues of the mirror in `.github/issues/`: 46 open and 78 closed. This pass accompanies moving state out of the issue bodies. The mirror contract keeps a body to intent, "without a paragraph about the current state of the code", and state lives in an issue review. Earlier passes had written `**Current state:**`, `**At present**`, `**Reassessment:**` and similar paragraphs into 113 bodies. They are removed, issue links become wiki links, 121 files change in all, and what the paragraphs said is re-derived and recorded here.

Reviewed revisions:

- `main`: `d8b0f4a` (`chore(project): sync the issue mirror`). Its application code is that of `98ad5bf`. The working tree carries an uncommitted infrastructure port (Go 1.27, workflows, docs site, release tooling). Of the application code, it changes only `go.mod` (the go directive and an `ignore` block) and `internal/model/github/contribution/helper_test.go`, neither of which a verdict below depends on.
- `fetcher`: `b0dd7d3` (`docs(status): explain push lock column and JSON filtering`), unmerged. It is cited as `fetcher:path:line` where an issue concerns its work.

Verdict rollup: relevant 28, partial 13, no longer relevant 74, needs clarification 2, defect confirmed 7; total 124.

| State | relevant | partial | no longer relevant | needs clarification | defect confirmed | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open | 28 | 8 | 2 | 2 | 6 | 46 |
| Closed | 0 | 5 | 72 | 0 | 1 | 78 |

The two open issues that are no longer relevant, [[issue-445]] and [[issue-446]], are done on `fetcher` only. The six closed issues that are not "no longer relevant" keep a residue that their closing did not cover, see [Recommendations](#recommendations).

## Dump integrity

`maintainer.py verify` against GitHub, after the rewritten bodies were published with `sync --yes` and read back with `dump`:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Issues | 124 files, 124 on GitHub; none without a file, none without an issue, none local-only |
| `body`, `title`, `labels`, `milestone`, `state`, `stateReason`, `updatedAt` | 0 differences each |
| Published | 122 bodies; [[issue-445]] and [[issue-446]] were unchanged |
| Redaction pending on GitHub | 0 |
| Comments | 45 notes, 45 on GitHub; no note without a URL, no dead URL, no body difference |
| Milestones | 2 files, 2 on GitHub; 0 differences |
| Wiki links on GitHub | 0 |

The notation is numbers (`issue-<n>`); `code` stays empty, and a code prefix is recommended for a shared vault. Every `[[issue-N]]` in the bodies resolves to a file and is published as `#N`. Twenty bodies link local notes as `../notes/…` (see [Related notes](#related-notes)). `.github/notes/` is ignored by git, so these links resolve only in a local checkout; on GitHub they stay dead relative links, deliberately, to name the note an issue rests on.

## Validation and sources

- Every issue file was read in full, together with the mirror SPEC and the review genre. Verdicts were derived from the code before the previous reviews were read; the comparison is in [Recommendations](#differences-from-the-previous-reviews).
- Code was read with `git show` and `git grep -n` on `d8b0f4a` and `b0dd7d3`. Fix commits of closed issues were located with `git log`. History before 2022-05-07 is squashed into `daab52c`, so [[issue-22]] and [[issue-23]] cannot be traced to individual commits.
- `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` pass on the working tree. On a copy of `fetcher`, the seven regression tests behind [[issue-445]] and [[issue-446]] pass (`go test ./internal/service/git ./internal/service/fetch -run 'PushURL|PushLock|ExistingTarget|OccupiedCloneTarget|EmptyRemote'`).
- Reproduced with a binary built from the working tree:
  - `github contribution lookup 2022` and a bare `lookup`, outside a git repository, print `recovered: assertion is not a true` and exit 1 ([[issue-155]]);
  - `github contribution diff` of two local snapshots with a 5 → 2 drop prints `+18446744073709551613` ([[issue-70]], [[issue-28]]);
  - `makefile build` assembles a three-level include chain in order, and two mutually including fragments exit 1 with `too many open files` ([[issue-81]]);
  - `github --help` lists only `contribution` ([[issue-80]]).
- Reproduced with scratch tests outside the repository, or through `go test -overlay`, which writes nothing into the tree:
  - a HEAD in the future (+2h, +26h, +400d) panics in `LookupRange(…).Until(now).Since(head)` ([[issue-133]], [[issue-148]]);
  - `ISOWeek` of Sunday 2024-12-29 is 52, so the label is `#53` ([[issue-284]]);
  - `FallbackDate` ignores `GIT_DIR` outside the work tree ([[issue-189]]);
  - `BuildHeatMap` returns zero counts for an unknown tooltip text ([[issue-90]]);
  - the `fill` loop never terminates for a package outside the module prefix ([[issue-6]], [[issue-21]]).
- Tags were listed locally and with one read-only `git ls-remote --tags origin`: `v0.1.0-rc1` to `v0.1.0-rc11`, no `v0.1.0`.
- Not checked:
  - live GitHub calls: `suggest` and `lookup` on real calendars, the time-zone scenarios, and [[issue-136]] end to end, which needs a token;
  - the `integration`-tagged tests;
  - CI history;
  - the go-tool template itself ([[issue-23]], [[issue-69]], [[issue-175]]);
  - the external upstreams (Linear, deps.dev, gonew, act, gh extensions);
  - whether go-git honours `GIT_DIR` through another API;
  - `fetcher` beyond the cited files and tests.

## Recommendations

### Defects to fix

| Defect | Issues | Location on `d8b0f4a` | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A decrease in `diff` wraps around | [[issue-70]], closed [[issue-28]] | `HeatMap` is `map[time.Time]uint` (`internal/model/github/contribution/heatmap.go:69`); `Diff` subtracts counts at `heatmap.go:112` | A signed delta type through `HeatMap.Diff` and `WeekReport`; identical on `fetcher` |
| A future HEAD panics in `suggest` | [[issue-133]], [[issue-148]] | Two paths reach the `from.Before(to)` assert in `NewRange` (`internal/pkg/time/range.go:11`, via `:105-106`): `Until(time.Now())` (`internal/command/github/contribution/suggest.go:40`) when the whole window lies in the future, as with +400 days, and `scope.Since(opts.Value)` (`suggest.go:46`) when only the anchor does | Clamp the anchor or return an error on both paths; test a future hour, day and year. One fix closes both issues |
| A bare date or no argument panics in `lookup` | [[issue-155]] | `Half=true` for an empty suffix (`internal/command/github/contribution/helper.go:122-124`) against `-1` weeks (`lookup.go:20`) and the assert in `range.go:17` | A consistent default. The documented `maintainer github contribution lookup` is affected too |
| `GIT_DIR` is ignored | [[issue-189]] | `git.PlainOpenWithOptions("", …)` (`helper.go:51`) silently falls back to now | Honour `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` or add `--git-dir`; report a failed open |
| Week label `#53` at the year boundary | [[issue-284]] | `week+1` (`helper.go:149`) | Derive the label from the week's Sunday consistently with `LookupRange` |
| Include cycles exhaust file descriptors | [[issue-81]] | `internal/command/makefile/entity.go:51`, `:73-79` | A visited set with a cycle error; resolve includes relative to the including file |
| `fill` never terminates outside the module prefix | none; blocks [[issue-21]] | `path.Dir(".")` stays `"."` (`internal/model/golang/vanity/issue6.go:18-21`) | Stop on `"."`, add a test case; open an issue or fold it into [[issue-21]] |

### Closed issues with a residue

- [[issue-28]]: its expected `5 → 3` gives `-2` still fails; the work continues in [[issue-70]].
- [[issue-40]]: `HeatMap.Range()` from the title was never added. Add it, guarding the empty map (`NewRange` asserts a non-zero `from`), or record that the requirement was dropped.
- [[issue-61]]: user-facing examples still show `->`. On `d8b0f4a` they are in `docs/readme.md:55-58, 101`; in the working tree they moved to `docs/content/changelog/index.md`. Fix the examples as part of the docs work.
- [[issue-90]], [[issue-150]], [[issue-220]]: on `main` three failures pass unnoticed or crash. A response without calendar cells becomes an empty calendar without an error (`heatmap.go:25-26, 65`; `internal/service/github/contribution.go:40-56`). An unrecognised tooltip becomes zero even when cells exist (`heatmap.go:52-54`). An unparsable date panics (`heatmap.go:31-34`). Each needs its own error: missing cells, a bad date, an unknown count. On `fetcher` the GraphQL calendar replaces scraping: a bad date returns an error and counts are typed, but an empty `weeks` collection still returns an empty calendar with a nil error (`fetcher:internal/service/github/contribution.go:109-121`). Merging it therefore leaves the empty-response check open.
- [[issue-174]]: the `integration`-tagged `TestService_FetchContributions` still expects 365 matches of the old SVG selectors in a live response (`internal/service/github/contribution_test.go:36-46`). It would fail against the table-only markup; it was not run here. The healthcheck runs `test`, not `test-integration`, so nothing notices. Update or drop that test.

### Open issues done or started on `fetcher`

- [[issue-445]] and [[issue-446]] are fulfilled on `fetcher` (`f753d7c`, `e537856`) and their regression tests pass. Close them when `fetcher` is merged.
- [[issue-64]] (calendar over GraphQL) and [[issue-98]] (`fetch` and `status`) are partial on `fetcher`. Before closing [[issue-64]], record the comparison of one period over GraphQL and HTML that its body asks for. [[issue-98]] keeps `upstream`/`fork-<owner>` remotes as its remaining requirement.
- The fix for [[issue-59]] (no-cache headers) disappears on `fetcher`. There the current-year query ends at the present second, so that a repeated query differs from what caches have seen (`fetcher:internal/service/github/contribution.go:93-99`). This is a cache-avoidance strategy, not a verified freshness guarantee: two calls within one second send identical variables. The body will then describe old behaviour; no action is needed on a closed issue.

### Release and maintenance

- [[issue-30]] and [[issue-69]]: tags stop at `v0.1.0-rc11` and the changelog is still "Unreleased". Decide whether `v0.1.0` ships from the current scope. If it does, pin the go-tool revision that [[issue-69]] means by "latest". If it does not, close [[issue-69]] in favour of [[issue-175]].
- [[issue-175]]: the mismatch it cites (Go 1.26 in `go.mod`, 1.21/1.22 in workflows) is real on `d8b0f4a`, and the uncommitted port moves everything to Go 1.27. Re-assess once it lands; what remains is likely documenting the intentional differences from the template.
- [[issue-39]]: titles still lack the `scope: subscope:` prefixes (for example [[issue-22]], [[issue-25]]).

### Merge, clarify or close

- [[issue-50]] and [[issue-51]] overlap. The `GitHub` interface and its mock (`internal/command/github/contract.go:11-21`) are ready: pass the service or a factory into the command constructors and use the mock in a test. Then close [[issue-51]] as covered or keep it only for the provider.
- [[issue-136]]: the lost date is the stdout/stderr split (`suggest.go:67-74`), and the counts follow from a schedule that is effectively UTC (`suggest.go:29`). Ask the reporter whether the wish is local working hours ([[issue-127]]) or a single-stream message; otherwise close.
- [[issue-17]] and [[issue-20]] were closed as duplicates, by their closing comments, but carry `stateReason: COMPLETED`; `DUPLICATE` would be accurate.

### Candidates for new issues

- `lookup /-5` inside a repository anchors on the HEAD commit, not on now (`helper.go:41-63`), which contradicts the usage comment `lookup /3 → now()/3` (`internal/command/github/contribution.go:66-67`). Fix the comment or the anchor.
- When no week has a gap, `Suggest` returns the lower bound with `Actual: 0` (`internal/model/github/contribution/suggest.go:66`), so the `nothing to suggest` branch (`suggest.go:47-49` of the command) is rarely reached.
- The jitter added after the schedule (`suggest.go:50`) can move a suggestion past now or out of the working hours; this is [[issue-193]]; see also [[issue-75]].

### Post-pass reconciliation

A second opinion by `gpt-6-astra` (low effort) read the body rewrite and this review after the pass. Its corrections landed in:

- bodies: the lost requirements and boundaries are restored in [[issue-8]], [[issue-25]], [[issue-31]], [[issue-36]], [[issue-41]], [[issue-58]], [[issue-150]] and [[issue-175]]; the state phrasing is removed from [[issue-41]], [[issue-47]], [[issue-58]] and [[issue-63]];
- [Defects to fix](#defects-to-fix): both panic paths of [[issue-133]];
- [Closed issues with a residue](#closed-issues-with-a-residue): separate errors for [[issue-90]], [[issue-150]] and [[issue-220]], the empty calendar on `fetcher`, and the unrun test of [[issue-174]];
- [Open issues done or started on `fetcher`](#open-issues-done-or-started-on-fetcher): the cache-avoidance wording for [[issue-59]];
- the table above: one row per issue.

The bodies were published to GitHub after the pass; [Dump integrity](#dump-integrity) shows the state after that.

It re-checked twelve `file:line` claims on `d8b0f4a` and confirmed them. The verdicts are unchanged and remain this review's own.
